questions: How many nanostring devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed the frequency jumps? The paper shows one device in three runs.
If other devices or runs exist, why were they set aside?

Which in-plane field ranges, sweep directions and temperatures did you measure beyond 12 to 30 mT and 18 to 35 mT at 85 mK, and what do the "extended field measurements" toward Bc2 (p. 5) show? The 0.25 mT spacing appears only between about 20 and 24 mT in Dataset 1; the other points sit 0.5 mT apart.

What does the second-best dataset look like, and did you repeat any field range within one cooldown? The two runs in Fig. 3(a) cover 12 to 20 mT and 20 to 30 mT, and both are referenced to their own 20 mT value; how was the offset between them, and so the 20.0 mT step, fixed?

The arrows at 12.0 mT and 18.0 mT sit on the first point of each run; what step do they mark? And a step at 22.5 mT appears in both cooldowns (with 20.0 and 20.5 mT close by); how often would that happen if entry fields were random?
Do the fitted flux offset ϕoff and critical current Ic change at the jump fields, and do the jumps appear in Ωm read directly at Φb = (n + 1/2)Φ0, without the Eq. (3) fit?

The step at 27.0 mT in Fig. 3(b) reads as about 0.95 × 10^9 Hz², which I convert to about 80 Hz at 5.8 MHz. How were the quoted 10 to 50 Hz step sizes obtained, and how did you decide that a step is one vortex, given that you also allow "one or a few flux quanta" (p. 4)?
Did you fit the junction asymmetry α, and how do k = 1.81 and the Labusch parameter change when α is left free?
